CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#644655: TightVNC and UltraVNC Viewer contains a heap-based buffer overflow
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

A heap-based buffer overflow exists in the Tight JPEG decoding component of the TightVNC Windows Viewer version 1.3.10 and affected UltraVNC Windows Viewers. An attacker controlling a malicious VNC server can trigger memory corruption by sending a specially crafted screen update. Successful exploitation can crash the viewer and may allow arbitrary code execution, although only denial of service conditions were demonstrated during testing.

Description

TightVNC and UltraVNC provide remote desktop access using the Remote Framebuffer (RFB) protocol. Their viewer applications connect to VNC servers and decode screen updates for local display. Tight encoding supports JPEG compression of image data within these updates.

The Windows viewer function DecompressJpegRect() allocates a heap buffer using a hardcoded maximum row width of 8,192 pixels but converts JPEG pixel data using the server-supplied rectangle width without adequately checking that the output fits within the buffer. A malicious server can supply an oversized Tight JPEG rectangle that causes the conversion loop to write beyond the allocated memory. In an allocation demonstrated during testing, which included 256 bytes of padding, the out-of-bounds write began at a rectangle width of 8,257 pixels.

Exploitation requires a vulnerable viewer to establish a session with an attacker-controlled or compromised VNC server and process its crafted update. The server can advertise a sufficiently large framebuffer, so checking that the rectangle fits within the advertised framebuffer does not, by itself, prevent this overflow. Authentication or transport encryption does not prevent exploitation by a malicious server participating in the session.

Impact

An attacker controlling a VNC server can corrupt heap memory in a connected vulnerable viewer, terminating the application and interrupting the remote desktop session. Memory corruption may also permit arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running the viewer, but only denial of service was confirmed during testing.

Solution

Review the Vendor Information section for product-specific patch information.

According to UltraVNC’s release notes, the Tight JPEG heap overflow vulnerability was addressed in version 1.8.2.8. Users should upgrade to a current supported release containing that fix, such as version 1.8.3.1.

Unfortunately, we were unable to reach TightVNC to coordinate a fix for the affected 1.3.10 Windows viewer. Users should replace affected viewers with a maintained version or an alternative solution that has been confirmed to address the vulnerability.

Until a corrected viewer is deployed, restrict connections to trusted VNC servers only. This reduces exposure but does not protect against a compromised trusted server.

Acknowledgements

Thank you to re9rch for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Michael Bragg.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#580079: Arbitrary file read/write vulnerability in ImageMagick-based applications with default configuration
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Multiple arbitrary file read and write vulnerabilities have been identified in applications that use ImageMagick with insufficiently restrictive security policies. Collectively referred to as ImageTragick2, these issues arise when ImageMagick processes attacker-controlled SVG or PostScript content using dangerous coders or delegates permitted by its default or application-supplied configuration. An attacker who can upload an image, or otherwise cause an application to process crafted image content, may be able to read or write files accessible to the ImageMagick process. In some deployments, these capabilities may be chained to achieve arbitrary code execution, compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected application and host.

Description

ImageMagick is a widely used open-source image-processing suite. Web and content-management applications, including Ruby on Rails, WordPress, MediaWiki, ownCloud Classic, and Redmine, may use ImageMagick for operations such as thumbnail generation, cropping, conversion, and transformation. ImageMagick is also commonly included in containerized AI image-processing pipelines. It may operate before inference to normalize or transform inputs, or after inference to convert and prepare generated output. In these environments, images may originate not only from direct uploads but also from URLs, automated agents, datasets, model outputs, or other upstream services.

Two vulnerability variants have been identified:
Coder invocation through SVG (MSL injection)

ImageMagick's SVG processing can allow a crafted SVG <image> element to invoke a dangerous coder through its xlink:href value, for example, by referencing an MSL: resource. ImageMagick may then interpret the referenced content as a Magick Scripting Language (MSL) script. The script can invoke additional image readers and direct attacker-controlled image data to selected filesystem paths, enabling unauthorized file access. Exploitation depends on the internal SVG coder and the required dangerous coders being available to the ImageMagick process.

Ghostscript invocation through content detection

ImageMagick's content-based format detection may identify crafted input as PostScript and invoke Ghostscript, a separate interpreter used by ImageMagick to handle PostScript, EPS, and PDF, even when the filename or declared type suggests another format. Although Ghostscript is invoked with -dSAFER, the observed configuration permits file access within /tmp. A crafted PostScript file may therefore read or write data in that directory. This can affect applications that use shared temporary storage for uploaded files, processing artifacts, sessions, or other security-sensitive data.

These issues highlight an important aspect of ImageMagick's security model: Behavior that can be restricted through a custom security policy is treated as a configuration issue, not a vulnerability in ImageMagick itself. Applications and distributions are therefore responsible for deploying a policy appropriate to their threat model. Many integrations, however, process untrusted content without a sufficiently restrictive policy.

Impact

An attacker who can cause an affected application to process crafted SVG or PostScript content may be able to read or write files in directory locations accessible to the ImageMagick process. In some cases, arbitrary code execution is possible when file access can be combined with writable executable content. AI-enabled services that utilize ImageMagick may face additional exposure because of untrusted image processing. In container deployments, writable host mounts, shared volumes, credentials, or inference artifacts can substantially increase the impact of a successful exploit.

Solution

Consult the Vendor Information section for product-specific updates and mitigations. Users of products that integrate ImageMagick, including Ruby on Rails, WordPress, MediaWiki, ownCloud Classic, and Redmine, should install vendor-provided updates when available. Updating ImageMagick alone may be insufficient if its security policy continues to permit dangerous coders or delegates.

Apply a custom policy.xml based on an allowlist: enable only the formats and operations the application requires, and disable unnecessary coders and delegates, including MSL, MVG, PS, EPS, and PDF. ImageMagick's bundled secure policy template may not be sufficient for every deployment; verify the effective policy and confirm that prohibited formats are rejected.

Additional recommendations include:
- Isolate image processing: Process untrusted images in a dedicated, minimally privileged environment with restricted filesystem access. Apply the same controls to AI preprocessing and post-processing pipelines.
- Validate and constrain input: Verify file content rather than relying on filenames, extensions, or client-supplied media types.
- Monitor processing activity: Alert on ImageMagick policy violations, unexpected delegate or coder use, unusual processing failures, and unexpected file creation.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to RyotaK of GMO Flatt Security Inc. for reporting these vulnerabilities. The pwn.ai team independently discovered Variant 2 and reported it to WordPress as CVE-2026-65640. This document was written by Vijay Sarvepalli and Molly Jaconski.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#685399: PromZard context key code injection leads to remote code execution
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

The npm library promzard, versions 4.0.0 and earlier, is vulnerable to remote code execution due to direct string interpolation of context object keys, which allows unsanitized JavaScript code injection.

Description

promzard is a Node.js library designed to automate configuration workflows by evaluating template modules and generating data objects via interactive prompting. The library allows users to provide a context object ctx to expose specific data to the template module.

promzard builds an object by walking the template module for prompt() and asynchronous functions. The keys of ctx, however, are treated as raw JavaScript source code instead of inert data. The implementation performs direct string interpolation of ctx keys, without validation or sanitization, into the parameter list of a function-expression source string that is then evaluated with vm.runInThisContext(). A key containing attacker-controlled JavaScript syntax can be executed during evaluation.

Impact

An attacker capable of influencing the ctx object’s keys (e.g. via parsed configuration file, an HTTP request, or environment variables) can break out of the function parameter list and inject arbitrary JavaScript code. This results in remote code execution within the context of the Node.js process.

Solution

Unfortunately, the maintainers of promzard could not be reached to coordinate the vulnerability. The CERT/CC recommends users ensure that any data used to populate ctx is strictly validated, and that arbitrary keys should not be passed from untrusted sources.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Abdullah Hamdan for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Alex Lewis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#944667: ComfyUI-Easy-Use contains unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

ComfyUI-Easy-Use version 1.4.1 and earlier contains a vulnerability in its save_preview() handler that allows an unauthenticated attacker to overwrite an installed custom node’s Python file. An attacker who can reach the affected ComfyUI instance over the network can use the overwrite to execute arbitrary code when ComfyUI restarts.

Description

ComfyUI is a node-based interface for building generative AI workflows. ComfyUI-Easy-Use is an extension that adds custom nodes and workflow utilities.
An attacker can upload a Python file to ComfyUI’s input directory then use save_preview() to copy that file over an installed custom node’s __init__.py. Upon restart, ComfyUI will import and execute the modified node. Remote exploitation requires a deployment that exposes the affected routes to the attacker without authentication.

Impact

An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the affected routes can execute arbitrary Python code and operating system commands with the privileges of the ComfyUI process. The attacker can read or modify models, workflows, and other files accessible to the process and obtain credentials available in its environment. Exploitation requires no user interaction. The reporter confirmed the vulnerability in ComfyUI-Easy-Use version up to verion 1.4.1.

Solution

Unfortunately, the maintainer of ComfyUI-Easy-Use could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability. To mitigate the vulnerability, remove the extension or restrict network access to ComfyUI to trusted users. The maintainer have released a fix in main as commit 8a0f2fc412.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Nguyen Huy Hoang for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Alex Lewis and Michael Bragg.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#188754: FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware contains multiple vulnerabilities
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Multiple vulnerabilities in the FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) may allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, disclosure of sensitive information, and full compromise of affected devices. Exploitation may enable an attacker to remotely control the rover, access audiovisual streams, or pivot into the user’s network.

Description

The FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ is a compact, internet‑connected mobile robot used in educational and consumer environments. The device includes a camera, microphone, motor controllers, and multiple onboard services. Multiple vulnerabilities in the EarthRover Mini+ firmware (version 6.2.4_6.2.5_0.614.0) can allow remote code execution, unauthorized access to onboard sensors, exposure of sensitive data, and complete device compromise. An attacker could potentially take remote control of the rover, access its audio and video streams, or use it to gain a foothold in its network.

CVE-2026-121685: The firmware contains several sets of hard-coded, fleet‑wide credentials, including BasicAuth credentials for an Agora token service, AWS IAM (Amazon Web Services Identity and Access Management) access keys, Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) credentials, and a Slack incoming webhook URL. Agora Token Service is an open source server that generates secure, time‑limited authentication tokens for use with Agora.io’s RTC (Real‑Time Communication) and RTM (Real‑Time Messaging) services. A Slack incoming webhook URL is a unique endpoint that lets external systems send messages into a Slack channel without the need for a full Slack application. These are embedded directly in frodobot.bin and are accessible through static analysis of the publicly downloadable firmware or from any device. Extraction requires no special privileges.

CVE-2026-121686: Unauthenticated remote command execution is allowed via Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT). A firmware method accepts arbitrary shell commands delivered via Amazon Web Services Internet of Things Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (AWS IoT MQTT) messages and executes them as root. Access is gated only by shared Internet of Things (IoT) credentials, with no per‑device authentication, enabling remote code execution (RCE) as root across the fleet. The IoT credentials are hard-coded in the firmware as discussed in CVE-2026-121685.

CVE-2026-121687: Several local interfaces are exposed without authentication. These services allow full local compromise of device functionality and provide access to sensitive information.
* HTTP REST API on port 80 (motor control, telemetry/GPS/IMEI) contains endpoints that reveal the plaintext Wi‑Fi password, enable Wi‑Fi join functionality, diagnostic export services
* Android Debug Bridge (ADB) root shell on port 5555
* SSH on port 22

CVE-2026-121688: The firmware contains an insecure STM32 update mechanism. STM32 is a family of 32-bit microcontrollers and is based primarily on Arm Cortex-M processor cores. They are widely used in embedded systems, IoT devices, industrial controls, robotics, automotive electronics, and consumer products. The STM32 motor‑controller firmware is fetched over unencrypted HTTP. Integrity is validated only via MD5, with the hash provided in the same unprotected response. No code‑signing mechanism is implemented, allowing firmware to be replaced with potentially malicious code.

CVE-2026-121689: The firmware exposes sensitive credentials through multiple insecure mechanisms. The Wi‑Fi PSK is stored in plaintext in wpa_supplicant.conf and is disclosed through unauthenticated API endpoints and diagnostic exports. Additionally, unauthenticated ADB access allows retrieval of the /etc/shadow file.

CVE-2026-121690: The firmware executes code with unnecessary privileges. All processes run as root and the system lacks privilege separation. The compromise of any single service results in full administrative control of the device.

Impact

Exploitation of these vulnerabilities may allow:
* Unauthorized access to live camera and microphone feeds.
* Fleet‑wide remote root access and full robot control via MQTT.
* Extraction of the user’s Wi‑Fi credentials and lateral movement onto the local network.
* Persistent compromise through tampered motor‑controller firmware.
* Unauthorized posting to the vendor’s Slack channels and potential exposure of backend infrastructure via IAM credential misuse.
* Given the rover’s mobility and sensor suite, exploitation may enable both digital and physical impacts.

Solution

As of this writing, the vendor has provided the following remediation status:

CVE-2026-121685 (Hard-coded credentials): Addressed

Most embedded credentials have been removed. One credential remains for requesting an Agora session token; backend authorization checks restrict misuse. Remaining credentials are limited to session‑bound operations.

CVE-2026-121686 (Remote command execution): Addressed

Arbitrary shell command execution has been removed. The device now supports only a small set of predefined management commands (e.g., reboot).

CVE-2026-121687 -- CVE-2026-121690. (Local interfaces and privilege model): Addressed or not remotely exploitable under current deployment model.

Local interfaces require connection to the device’s Wi‑Fi access point, which has a configurable password. The vendor asserts that an attacker must be physically near the device and connected to its Wi‑Fi network to exploit these interfaces. The firmware update process is manual and conducted through the local Wi‑Fi network.

The vendor validated changes via static analysis and internal implementation review, and considers the findings fixed, mitigated, or not applicable in the current deployment model.

Users are encouraged to update to the latest version of the FrodoBots EarthRover Mini+ firmware.

Acknowledgements

Thank you to Justin Davis for reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Bob Kemerer.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#385711: PrestaShop debug mode configuration allows PHP code injection
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

PrestaShop's back-office Performance > Debug mode functionality contains a PHP code injection vulnerability. An authenticated attacker with permission to modify debug-mode configuration can submit crafted cookie configuration values that are written into an executable PHP configuration file. Successful exploitation could allow arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the PHP process.

Description

PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform for creating and managing online stores. Its back-office Performance configuration includes a Debug mode for developers, which is enabled based on a specified cookie name and value.

PrestaShop's debug-mode configuration code inserts the user-controlled values debug_cookie_name and debug_cookie_value into a PHP expression without adequately escaping or sanitizing them for use in PHP source code. The application writes this expression into the PHP define() statement in config/defines.inc.php or config/defines_custom.inc.php. A crafted value can terminate the intended string and introduce attacker-controlled PHP statements. The modified configuration file is loaded during application initialization, causing the injected code to execute on a subsequent request.

Exploitation requires an authenticated back-office account with permission to modify debug mode settings and a configuration file writable by the PHP process. Root or operating-system administrator privileges are not required. Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) protection helps prevent unauthorized requests made through another user's session, but does not prevent exploitation by an attacker controlling an account with the required permissions. Injected code executes with the privileges of the PHP process. Affected release versions remain to be confirmed.

Impact

An authenticated attacker with the required configuration permissions could execute arbitrary PHP code in the security context of the PHP process. This could allow access to application secrets and customer data, modification or deletion of application files and database contents, and disruption of store operations. Operating-system command execution depends on the PHP configuration and available functions. The vulnerability does not independently grant root privileges.

Solution

PrestaShop version 9.2.1 addresses this vulnerability. Administrators should upgrade affected installations to version 9.2.1 or later.
If an immediate upgrade is not possible, allow only trusted administrators to modify Performance and Debug mode settings, and restrict network access to the back office. Where operationally feasible, prevent the PHP process from writing to config/defines.inc.php and config/defines_custom.inc.php. This may also prevent legitimate configuration changes.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Deflask13 for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Michael Bragg.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#124705: BaseChat – Audio Dating App, Android version 9.8.1, contains multiple vulnerabilities
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the Android application, BaseChat – Audio Dating App, version 9.8.1, which ultimately compromise the privacy of users’ personal data and activity.

Description

BaseChat is an online dating platform built in Flutter and targeted toward users over 18. It facilitates anonymous, voice-first interaction between users. Three distinct vulnerabilities have been identified within the shipped Android application.
VU#124705.1: The application fails open when validating TLS server certificates for connections to its backend API host. The application allows any self-signed certificate to bypass standard TLS security checks.
VU#124705.2: Paid user accounts are mapped to a third-party RevenueCat subscriber database using raw MSISDNs (phone numbers), which are a guessable public identifier. Because the RevenueCat Software Development Kit (SDK) includes a public API key within the application’s Android Package Kit (APK), an attacker can query the RevenueCat’s API using predictable identifiers to retrieve individual user metadata.
VU#124705.3: The application writes Personally Identifiable Information (PII) to Android system logs in its production build. During voice calls, the application logs the remote party’s MSISDN through unstripped debug statements, which allows an attacker to recovery phone numbers of callers who are intended to remain anonymous.

Impact

Impacts of successful exploitation vary by vulnerability.
VU#124705.1: A network-positioned attacker can intercept and modify API communication, potentially leading to account takeover via session credential theft.
VU#124705.2: An attacker can locate the public RevenueCat SDK key and query the RevenueCat API using arbitrary phone numbers to retrieve associated user metadata, including activity and purchase history.
VU#124705.3: The personal data, or PII, of other users, intended to be anonymous, can be accessed through local system logs. The application’s backend sending other users’ MSISDNs to the client in any capacity presents a privacy violation.
These vulnerabilities have been confirmed against Basechat – Audio Dating App, Android version 9.8.1.

Solution

Unfortunately, Mobile Trading GmbH, the owners of BaseChat, could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Mahmoud Ali Khan for reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Alex Lewis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#203719: INFINITT PACS System Manager contains multiple code execution vulnerabilities
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

INFINITT PACS installations using System Manager versions 3.0.11.3 and 3.0.11.5 contain vulnerabilities that may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code. INFINITT Healthcare has remediated the issues in System Manager versions 3.0.12.3 and 3.0.12.5.

Description

INFINITT PACS is an enterprise web-based medical imaging platform that stores, retrieves, and displays patient scans.

CVE-2026-16305
An improperly protected update manifest may allow a local attacker to execute commands with administrative privileges when an update is approved.
SmartExecute.exe reads and runs commands from execlist.txt after an update. Because of insecure file permissions on execlist.txt, a low-privileged attacker can modify the file before it is processed to add arbitrary malicious commands. After SmartUpdate.exe launches, it runs SmartExecute.exe and the user can be prompted by User Account Control (UAC), which can allow the malicious command to execute with administrative privileges.

CVE-2026-16306
An unsafe command dispatch through the registered imodular:// URI scheme may result in code execution.
A vulnerability in IModular.exe allows an attacker to execute certain application functions by supplying a crafted imodular:// link. The application reads the cmd value from the link and executes the corresponding function without verifying that the command is permitted or safe. By convincing an end user to open a crafted imodular:// link, an attacker can cause IModular.exe to access attacker-controlled files or run specific programs from a local folder or network share. The link also accepts a url parameter that causes IModular.exe to connect to an attacker-controlled SignalR endpoint, creating an unauthorized outbound connection.

Impact

Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-16305 may allow a local, low-privileged attacker to execute arbitrary commands with administrative privileges on the affected workstation. An attacker could then install or modify software, access protected files, disable security controls, or establish persistent access to the system.
Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-16306 may allow a remote attacker to execute code with the privileges of the affected user, access or modify data available to that user, and use the compromised workstation as a foothold for further attacks. The vulnerability may allow unauthorized outbound communication with an attacker-controlled SignalR server, potentially exposing sensitive information or enabling additional malicious activity.

Solution

There are no indications that these vulnerabilities have been exploited. INFINITT Healthcare recommends upgrading affected installations to one of the following fixed System Manager versions:

  • System Manager 3.0.12.3
  • System Manager 3.0.12.5

Organizations should apply the appropriate update as soon as operationally feasible.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to Piotr Berlinski from CyberArms.io for identifying these vulnerabilities, and to INFINITT for quickly addressing the problems. This document was written by Michael Bragg.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#701544: Retraction of mpc-lib hardened derivation fails to protect ancestor isolation
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Fireblocks' mpc-lib library contains a cryptographic fail-open vulnerability in its BIP32 hardened derivation implementation in the case of a missing private parent key. This breaks the ancestor isolation property of hardened derivation, allowing an attacker with a compromised lower-level signer share to recover the higher-level share it was derived from.

After reviewing the feedback from Fireblocks and further analysis of the case, we have determined that this does not constitute a valid vulnerability. Fireblocks clarified that mpc-lib's signing protocols use only non-hardened BIP32 derivation and that a hardened index is handled as a non-hardened one. Effective exploitation would require privileged access, at which point the attacker would already hold the master share, rendering the issue moot.

Description

Fireblocks is a digital-asset custody and wallet platform that secures the private keys behind cryptocurrency wallets for institutions and exchanges, using multi-party computation (MPC) so that no single machine ever holds a complete key.

Fireblocks’ key security pipeline contains two layers: MPC, which splits a single key into shares, and hardened derivation, which mathematically isolates each share from its key hierarchy. Normally, the derivation delta between parent and child keys is formed by hashing the private parent key, a derivation index, and associated metadata.

VU#701544.1
A fail-open vulnerability was identified within the BIP32 hardened derivation implementation which fails to reject operations where no parent secret is present. If a parent key is missing, the implementation substitutes the secret parent contribution with a null buffer. Because the buffer becomes a known constant, 0, the delta becomes computable, violating ancestor isolation.

Impact

An attacker who compromises a single MPC party's descendant signer share, and who knows the associated chain code, can compute the public derivation delta and subtract it to recover that party's ancestor share, repeating the operation up the hierarchy to obtain that party's root share. The isolation between derivation levels is reduced to a publicly computable scalar, so a single leaf-level share compromise extends to that party's shares across the entire key hierarchy managed by the MPC cluster.

The primary MPC secret-sharing layer still prevents reconstruction of a full private key from a single compromised party's shares, so this flaw does not by itself yield a spendable key. Its significance is the elimination of a defense-in-depth layer: hardened derivation no longer provides post-compromise ancestor isolation, threshold-security assumptions degrade as compromise propagates across derivation levels over time, and the downgrade occurs silently with no error or log signal. In BIP32 deployments where the chain code is treated as public, the precondition of knowing the chain code is trivially met.

Solution

At the time of writing, Fireblocks could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability, and no vendor fix is available. Integrators can, however, reduce exposure with the following mitigations.

  • Treat the chain code as secret. The attack is only available to a party that knows the chain code, because the derivation delta is computed as HMAC-SHA512(chaincode, ...). Chain codes should not be distributed in watch-only extended public keys or otherwise exposed to untrusted parties. Where a deployment can keep the chain code confidential, the delta is no longer publicly computable and ancestor-share recovery is not possible. This is the most effective mitigation available without a code change.

  • Do not rely on hardened derivation for isolation between signer shares. Audit derivation paths for hardened segments and treat the compromise of any single share as potentially exposing that party's other shares across the derivation hierarchy.

A complete fix requires a change in the library.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to hodlturk for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written using AI assisted tools by Alexander Curtis and Alex Lewis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#128947: COVESA vsomeip excessive memory allocation in reliable (TCP) endpoint buffer handling
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

vsomeip, COVESA's open source implementation of the SOME/IP automotive communication middleware, contained a memory allocation vulnerability present in versions 3.7.3 and below. A vsomeip reliable (TCP) SOME/IP endpoint grows its receive buffer to an attacker-declared message size before validating that the declared bytes have actually been received, allowing a remote, unauthenticated peer to exhaust host memory and deny service. The issue was reported publicly as COVESA/vsomeip issue #1009 and fixed in release 3.7.4 (2026-07-06).

Description

CVE-2026-91141
vsomeip is a middleware implementation of the Scalable service-Oriented MiddlewarE over IP (SOME/IP) protocol, widely used for service-oriented communication between electronic control units (ECUs) in automotive and other embedded environments. A SOME/IP message begins with a 16-byte header that includes a 32-bit length field declaring the size of the message that follows.

A vulnerability was discovered in the handling of this length field on reliable (TCP) endpoints. When a message arrives, vsomeip grows its receive buffer to the size declared in the length field in order to read the incoming message, before confirming that those bytes have actually been received. In the default configuration, no size limit is applied to reliable endpoints, so a peer can declare a message size of up to roughly 4 GB and cause the receiver to allocate that memory. Because a freshly accepted connection reaches this path on its first message, no valid service, credentials, or SOME/IP authentication are required to trigger the allocation. The client endpoint contains the same behavior, where a malicious or compromised server can attack a connecting client.

Deployments that explicitly configure a reliable message-size limit are not affected.

This issue is publicly known. It was reported as COVESA/vsomeip issue #1009 (opened 2026-02-26) and fixed in release 3.7.4 (released 2026-07-06).

Impact

A remote, unauthenticated peer can force the host to allocate an attacker-chosen amount of memory, up to approximately 4 GB per connection, by sending a single short message on a normal TCP connection to any reachable reliable SOME/IP endpoint in the default configuration. On a memory-constrained node this can terminate the service outright: a service limited to 1.5 GB was OOM-killed by a single 16-byte message claiming a 3 GB payload. On a memory-rich host, the allocation for a single connection is released when the connection closes, so sustained memory exhaustion and denial of service follow from holding or repeating connections, each forcing its own allocation.

Solution

Upgrade to vsomeip 3.7.4 or later. This issue is fixed in release 3.7.4 (released 2026-07-06). The fix replaces the unlimited compile-time default (MESSAGE_SIZE_UNLIMITED) with a bounded DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE of 10 MiB, so reliable endpoints reject an oversized declared length before growing the receive buffer even when no limit is explicitly configured. The release also adds a regression test for an oversized length field. The issue and fix are tracked publicly in COVESA/vsomeip issue #1009.

Deployments that cannot upgrade immediately should apply the following mitigations.

  • Deployments can explicitly set max-payload-size-reliable (or the equivalent per-service reliable message-size limit) to a value appropriate for the service. Endpoints with such a limit configured reject oversized declared lengths and are not affected by this issue. This is the most effective mitigation available without upgrading.

  • Because the vulnerability is reachable by any host that can open a TCP connection to a reliable SOME/IP endpoint, exposure should be minimized through network segmentation. Reliable endpoints should be confined to trusted, isolated in-vehicle or lab networks, and firewall or access-control rules should limit connectivity to known, authorized peers. SOME/IP endpoints should never be exposed to untrusted or external networks.

  • Operators should monitor for anomalous memory growth on services offering reliable endpoints and for unexpected or repeated inbound TCP connections to SOME/IP ports, which may indicate attempts to exploit this vulnerability.

Acknowledgements

Thank you to the Jaafer Rahmani for reporting this vulnerability. This document was written by Alexander Curtis.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#763488: Memory corruption vulnerabilities in PHP
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

Two memory-related vulnerabilities have been identified in PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. An unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to PHP web services can exploit these vulnerabilities via specially crafted HTTP requests to potentially achieve arbitrary code execution.

Description

PHP is a widely used open-source scripting language designed for web development and server-side applications. It powers millions of websites and web applications worldwide and can be deployed through a variety of server configurations, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed.

CVE-2026-109618: A memory corruption vulnerability exists in the out-of-memory (OOM) handling mechanism of PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. The vulnerability occurs when an OOM condition interrupts request processing while internal request data is only partially initialized; subsequent cleanup routines may access the invalid memory, potentially causing memory corruption and enabling arbitrary code execution.

CVE-2026-109619: A use-after-free vulnerability exists in the global state management of PHP versions prior to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, and 8.5.12. The vulnerability occurs when a worker retains a reference to request-owned state after its backing memory has been freed. A subsequent request handled by the same worker can access this stale state before normal request initialization resets it, potentially causing memory corruption and enabling arbitrary code execution.

Impact

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities allows an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute arbitrary code via specially crafted HTTP requests, compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the web service and underlying infrastructure. Apache mod_php deployments are at particularly high risk, as proof-of-concept exploitation has demonstrated that unauthenticated requests can trigger the attack before any application code executes.

Solution

Refer to the Vendor Information section below for newly patched versions of PHP that remediate these vulnerabilities. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately to PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, or 8.5.12. Source downloads are available on the official PHP release page at php.net/downloads.

Linux users are advised to check with their distribution vendor for updated packages, as many distributions received patches in advance. For PHP 8.1 and older versions that no longer receive official updates from the PHP project, contact your LTS vendor for backported fixes or upgrade to a supported version. The PHP security team has provided limited source backports for PHP 7.4, PHP 8.0, and PHP 8.1 to assist users building from source or without access to an LTS vendor.

If immediate patching is not feasible, the following temporary mitigation measures may reduce exposure to specific attack paths, though they do not provide complete protection. Because these vulnerabilities are closely related, mitigations for both CVEs should be applied:

For CVE-2026-109618 (OOM Corruption):

  • Set memory_limit=-1 at an administrative level so it cannot be overridden by applications, for example via php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration.
  • Set a low post_max_size (8M for applications without file uploads, 32M if uploads are necessary).
  • Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size.
  • Enforce limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request-body size, input variable count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth.
  • Use container or cgroup limits as an availability boundary with policies that kill only the affected worker. Notably, RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA should not be used to bound memory, as these cause mmap() to fail once the limit is reached, triggering the vulnerable code path rather than preventing it.

For CVE-2026-109619 (Stale Global State):

  • Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 in php.ini, FPM pool, or server configuration and restart all workers.
  • On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart all workers.
  • Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization.
  • Remediate attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts.

System owners can limit the potential impact of successful exploitation by implementing network segmentation and ensuring that PHP installations are configured to run with minimum necessary privileges. Users are advised to monitor closely for unusual PHP process behavior or unexpected memory allocation patterns.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to OpenAI, Wiz, and Ryan at Calif.io for reporting these vulnerabilities. This document was written by Molly Jaconski.

CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.title: VU#645818: Xerj Console API authentication bypass leads to unauthorized credential minting
CERT/CC Vulnerability Notes.description:
Overview

An authentication bypass vulnerability in the Xerj Console API allows sessions to bypass passkey-backed requirements during token issuance. By exploiting this flaw, an attacker with an existing valid token can create independent, persistent successor credentials directly through the console API. This allows the attacker to maintain access and potentially escalate privileges within the Xerj ecosystem, even if the initial token is revoked.

Description

Xerj is an open-source search and indexing engine tailored specifically for AI agents utilizing the Elasticsearch API, allowing AI models to query a structured index.

The vulnerability, CVE-2026-97406, stems from a flaw in how session states are authenticated and handled within the Xerj system architecture. According to the documented security contract, the issuance of new API tokens must be strictly authorized by a passkey-backed session. However, the Xerj implementation converts both standard browser sessions and API bearer tokens into the same generic AuthSession object. The token creation handler then accepts this generalized principal without verifying whether the session was authenticated via a passkey.
Because of this architectural oversight, an attacker who obtains or intercepts a valid Xerj API token can directly invoke the token creation endpoint, allowing them to create independent successor credentials with the same access levels of the original token. Furthermore, the Xerj platform lacks hierarchical revocation logic; consequently, revoking a compromised parent token has no effect on any descendant tokens spawned from it.

Impact

Exploiting this vulnerability allows an attacker to gain persistent, unauthorized access that completely bypasses multi-factor controls. The security risk escalates significantly if the compromised token belongs to a Xerj account owner. In this scenario, the newly created successor token retains full administrative authority. An attacker can use this persistent access to issue a new account invitation, redeem it in their own browser, and successfully enroll an entirely independent, attacker-controlled passkey. This grants the attacker permanent control over the Xerj instance and its sensitive data indices, rendering the revocation of the initial token completely ineffective.

Solution

The vendor could not be reached to coordinate this vulnerability and an official patch has not been made available at the time of this writing. Users are advised to monitor the project's GitHub repository for updates and install the latest version of this library once a fix has been released.

Acknowledgements

Thanks to the reporter, Shiran Guez, a Principal Application Security Architect.

This document was written by Laurie Tyzenhaus.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-020: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 12 November 2026, the Cloud Software Group published security bulletins for its Citrix products addressing 28 memory flaws in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway. One of these vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-120868, affects every deployment, including those using the default configuration. The vendor bulletin describes the impact as unpredictable behaviour and denial of service.
Citrix reports no exploitation, and no public proof-of-concept has been confirmed. CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading all customer-managed NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliances to the fixed releases. Internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances should be upgraded first.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
CERT-EU.description:
On 20 October 2026, the PHP project announced an upcoming security release addressing two critical vulnerabilities in PHP. Public reports indicated that these vulnerabilities could lead to remote code execution (RCE).
The PHP team released the fixes today, 21 October 2026 at 13:30 UTC, in PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. Both vulnerabilities can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Technical details are now being discussed publicly, and initial proofs of concept (PoCs) have begun to circulate. This raises the likelihood that attackers are already exploiting the vulnerabilities.
[New] On 23 October, PHP disclosed a new RCE vulnerability. However, it affects only web applications configured in an unusual way, and PHP considers it an unlikely risk. PHP will not issue an out-of-band release for this vulnerability. Instead, organisations are advised to apply mitigation to fully protect from this RCE vector.
CERT-EU advises organisations to patch affected assets immediately. Where that is not feasible, organisations should consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is applied and verified.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
CERT-EU.description:
On 21 October 2026, GitLab published a security advisory addressing several vulnerabilities among which a critical flaw that could allow an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on a GitLab server.
CERT-EU recommends organisations to update affected assets as soon as possible, prioritising internet facing assets, and to run an assessment to identify compromised assets.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 14 October 2026, Cisco published a security advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting the Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway. This vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system.
The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability.
CERT-EU strongly recommends updating the Content Scanner Tools package or upgrading Cisco AsyncOS Software to a fixed release as soon as possible, prioritising appliances reachable from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking all affected appliances for indicators of compromise.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-016: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab CE and EE
CERT-EU.description:
On 12 October 2026, GitLab released versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8 of GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE), fixing 24 security issues among which a critical vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading self-managed GitLab CE/EE instances to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with internet-facing instances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-015: Critical Vulnerability in Multiple Atlassian Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 5 October 2026, Atlassian published a security advisory addressing a critical arbitrary file access vulnerability. It affects Bitbucket Data Center, Confluence Data Center, Jira Service Management Data Center, Jira Software Data Center, Bamboo Data Center, Crowd Data Center, Crucible and Fisheye.
CERT-EU strongly recommends upgrading all affected installations to a fixed version as soon as possible, starting with instances accessible from the internet. CERT-EU also recommends checking access logs for signs of exploitation.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-014: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway
CERT-EU.description:
On 27 September 2026, Citrix published a security bulletin addressing 8 vulnerabilities affecting customer-managed Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway, among which 2 critical unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Citrix has confirmed active exploitation of these 2 critical vulnerabilities in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends updating affected software and running a compromise assessment on those exposed on the internet.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-013: Critical Vulnerability in F5 BIG-IP APM
CERT-EU.description:
On 22 September 2026, F5 published an advisory addressing a critical vulnerability affecting its BIG-IP APM product. The vendor confirmed active exploitation in the wild.
CERT-EU recommends taking appropriate actions as soon as possible.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
CERT-EU.description:
On 9 September 2026, Check Point released emergency security updates addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting Check Point Security Gateway, Security Management Server, and Spark Firewall deployments configured to use Remote Access VPN or Site-to-Site VPN. Both vulnerabilities carry a CVSS score of 9.8 and could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to execute arbitrary code on affected appliances.
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying the available hotfixes as soon as possible, prioritising internet-facing and perimeter appliances.

CERT-EU.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
CERT-EU.description:
On 8 September 2026, as part of its September Security Patch Day, SAP released Security Notes addressing two critical vulnerabilities affecting a broad range of SAP products[3]. The most severe, CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), is a memory corruption vulnerability in SAP Extended Passport (EPP) processing, nicknamed "OVERPASS" by the Onapsis Research Labs (ORL), which discovered and responsibly disclosed it[3]. The second, CVE-2026-58240 (CVSS 9.8), nicknamed "S4GET", is a missing authentication check in the SAP NetWeaver Message Server[6].
Both are remotely exploitable without authentication. According to the reporting researchers, successful exploitation of either can result in arbitrary operating system command execution under the account that owns the SAP installation, leading to full compromise of the affected system and the business data it holds[6].
CERT-EU strongly recommends applying SAP Security Notes 3747649 and 3759472 as soon as possible.

Microsoft Security Update Guide.title: CVE-2026-100223 Windows NTFS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Microsoft Security Update Guide.description:
An elevation of privilege vulnerability exists when reparse points are created by sandboxed processes allowing sandbox escape. An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could use the sandbox escape to elevate privileges on an affected system. 

To exploit the vulnerability, an attacker would first have to log on to the system, and then run a specially crafted application to take control over the affected system.

The security update addresses the vulnerability by preventing sandboxed processes from creating reparse points targeting inaccessible files.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-18742
CVE.report.description: The Flatsome theme for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via 'data-text-sec', 'data-title', and 'title' Attributes via Custom HTML Block in all versions up to, and including, 3.20.12 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload survives server-side sanitization because wp_kses_post permits data-* attributes globally via _wp_add_global_attributes, allowing attacker-controlled values in data-text-sec, data-title, and title attributes to persist in saved post content and be later interpreted as HTML by the ux-countdown, scroll-to, and lightbox-gallery JavaScript behaviors.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129319
CVE.report.description: create-ecdh is a browserifiable implementation of Node.js crypto.createECDH. In versions 4.0.4 and below, the JavaScript implementation (browser.js, used by browser bundlers and on Node.js versions without a working native crypto.createECDH) did not validate peer public keys in ECDH.prototype.computeSecret or ECDH.prototype.setPublicKey. The peer point was multiplied by the local private key without checking that it was on the configured curve or in its prime-order subgroup. An attacker who can submit public keys to a party that reuses a static private key can perform an invalid-curve or small-subgroup attack and recover the private key modulo small factors, eventually recovering the full key via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. For the ed25519 and curve25519 curves, low-order points were also accepted, which could force a predictable shared secret. On modern Node.js, create-ecdh re-exports the native implementation, which is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.5.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126697
CVE.report.description:
The Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 was distributed with a hidden update mechanism that fetched Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 updates from its author's own server instead of WordPress.org, which was used to push a backdoored build to sites, allowing the attacker controlling that server to inject arbitrary content into pages and to deliver arbitrary code to affected sites.

Version 5.2.1, as published on WordPress.org, bundled the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker library (updater/ directory) configured to poll https://anadnet.com/updates/?action=get_metadata&slug=quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4. In March 2021 that server delivered a modified 5.2.3 build, different from the 5.2.3 later published on WordPress.org, which kept the update channel and added a the_content filter that, for logged-out visitors on single posts and pages, fetched content from https://w.anadnet.com/bro/3/ (passing the site host, request URI and visitor User-Agent) and prepended the response to the post (observed serving SEO spam links to search engine crawlers). Because the version string matched a later WordPress.org release, affected sites were not offered a clean update until 5.2.4.

Indicators of compromise:
- Outbound requests to anadnet.com or w.anadnet.com
- An updater/ directory (Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 Update Checker, Puc v4p10) inside wp-content/Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4/
- The strings filter_the_content_in_the_main_loop, ppr_pro, QQQEND or w.anadnet.com in page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php
- page_post_redirect_Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4.php with MD5 ad717da18cf8a2b69899c0d7dafee05a (tampered 5.2.3)

Remediation: remove the Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 (it has been closed on WordPress.org), or at minimum reinstall the clean 5.2.4 from WordPress.org, delete any leftover updater/ directory, verify the files with "wp Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4 verify-checksums quick-pagepost-redirect-Quick Page/Post Redirect Plugin WordPress plugin before 5.2.4", clear the opcode cache, and treat any site that ran the tampered build as potentially compromised.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-123122

This is a regression of CVE-2025-4212, reintroduced in 2.4.0.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-119258

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118183
CVE.report.description: The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check whether a user may publish posts when duplicating one, allowing users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributors, to create published posts, including posts attributed to other users.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118182
CVE.report.description: The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not check that a user duplicating a post is allowed to edit it, which, when the slug takeover option is enabled, allows users of a role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, such as Contributor, to move any readable post off its permalink and publish their copy at that address.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118181
CVE.report.description: The Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 does not perform a capability check when saving its global settings, relying only on its own role-access list, which allows users of any role an administrator has given Duplicate Post WordPress plugin before 1.5.8 access to, as low as Subscriber, to overwrite those settings, including the role-access list itself.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117490
CVE.report.description: The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not enforce the acting user's publish and post-type restrictions on an AJAX save action, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to publish their own content and change its post type (for example to a product) without holding the required capabilities.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117487
CVE.report.description: The Flatsome WordPress theme before 3.20.13 does not perform a capability or nonce check on an AJAX action available to unauthenticated users, and does not restrict the status of the posts it returns by ID, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the content of unpublished (draft and pending) posts.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-125709
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in libstdc++. When a byte-by-byte write operation fails during file stream processing, the library may still append data into the internal memory buffer. An attacker capable of inducing repeated write failures in an affected service can trigger a buffer overflow, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) or memory corruption.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116528
CVE.report.description: The Chargely Free Subscriptions For Woocommernce WordPress plugin through 1.0 does not perform any authorization check on a REST API route that returns its stored configuration, allowing unauthenticated attackers to retrieve the live WooCommerce REST API consumer key and secret it holds, which grant read and write access to the whole store.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111034
CVE.report.description: The Countdown, Coming Soon, Maintenance  WordPress plugin through 3.0.8 does not check that the user is allowed to browse content before returning post titles from one of its AJAX actions, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to list the titles of published entries of any post type, including types that WordPress does not expose to them. Draft, private and pending content is not returned; only published entries are disclosed.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-111033
CVE.report.description: The Countdown, Coming Soon, Maintenance  WordPress plugin through 3.0.8 does not perform authorization or nonce checks when saving countdown data on post save, and its output-sanitization allowlist permits script tags, allowing users with Author-level access and above to store arbitrary web scripts that execute when the affected content is viewed on the front end or in an administrator session.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-105984
CVE.report.description: The Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5 does not perform authorization or capability checks on several of its AJAX actions, allowing unauthenticated users to destroy its stored configuration and delete its records.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-105983
CVE.report.description: The Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5 does not perform authorization or capability checks on several of its AJAX actions and REST routes, allowing unauthenticated users to disclose the Email Marketing 4Dem WordPress plugin through 2.0.5's stored configuration and data and to modify its stored settings.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126173
CVE.report.description: The AutomatorWP Pro plugin for WordPress' webhook addon is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.4. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to reset the password of any WordPress account, including administrators, resulting in full account takeover. This is only exploitable when an administrator has configured an automation pairing a Receive Webhook trigger — with an 'Is the user ID' field — to an Update-User action whose User ID field is left blank and whose Password field is mapped to the webhook password tag, which is a documented, supported plugin configuration.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124969
CVE.report.description: The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the replace_urls_in_value function in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires PEAR's Archive_Tar library to be present and loadable on the host (common in official WordPress Docker images and many PHP distributions), and an administrator must subsequently use the plugin's Rename control on any attachment after the attacker has staged a malicious payload in a comment. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124703

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-124702

CVE.report.description: In Telerik UI for WinForms, versions prior to 2026.4.1111, a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability exists that allows an attacker to perform unauthorized actions in the context of the affected application.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120150
CVE.report.description: Use after free in PostgreSQL expanded-record domain checks allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via repeated checks of a domain over a composite type that cause reuse of a dangling memory-context pointer.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120149
CVE.report.description: Heap-based buffer overflow in PostgreSQL foreign batch inserts allows a foreign server to execute arbitrary code, via reporting that it inserted more rows than the server supplied.  postgres_fdw can legitimately encounter this when a rule on the remote table expands an INSERT into additional rows.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120148
CVE.report.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL extended statistics allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via a statistics expression of an anonymous RECORD type whose backend-local type identifier denotes a different row type in another session.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120147
CVE.report.description: Use after free in the PostgreSQL dblink extension allows an object creator to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via type conversion code that re-enters dblink and closes a connection whose results an outer dblink call is reading.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120145
CVE.report.description: Missing authorization in PostgreSQL logical replication allows a compromised publisher to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the superuser-owned subscription, via naming a system catalog as a replication target.  Only subscriptions owned by a superuser are vulnerable.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116330
CVE.report.description: Untrusted data inclusion in PostgreSQL pg_dump tar-format restore.sql allows a compromised origin server to execute arbitrary code as the client operating system account running psql, via the predictable restriction key in restore.sql.  This is a gap in the fix for CVE-2025-8714.  restore.sql is undocumented.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20, and 14.25 are affected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116329
CVE.report.description: Type confusion in PostgreSQL statistics import allows a table maintainer to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via nested SET DATA TYPE during conversion of values to import.  Within major version 18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116328
CVE.report.description: Integer wraparound in PostgreSQL generation memory contexts allows a database user to execute arbitrary code as the operating system user running the database, via freeing an allocation larger than 1 GB and causing its block to be reused for smaller chunks whose back-pointer offset cannot represent that position.  Within major versions 16-18, minor versions before PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, and 16.16 are affected.  Versions before PostgreSQL 16 are unaffected.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-116326
CVE.report.description: Uncaught exceptions in PostgreSQL plperl allow an object creator to cause use of a stale sigjmp_buf, via a tied Perl object, or a Perl object whose overloaded conversion throws while plperl is handling another error. CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-114569
CVE.report.description:
OriginLab Origin Viewer OGWU File Parsing Heap-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of OriginLab Origin Viewer. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of OGWU files. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a heap-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-30430.
